subject: Demo: Dedicated capacity for Finlytics — throughput & latency requirements
messages:
From: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@finlytics.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in Dedicated for low-latency trading use case

Hi Marissa,

I signed up for Redwood earlier this week and have been running some quick experiments with the hosted API. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production trading feature and would like to schedule a deep-dive demo focused on throughput & latency.

Short background: Finlytics runs real-time pricing models that require consistent p95 latency under 75ms for 512-token requests and sustained throughput of ~120 concurrent requests (roughly 30qps sustained with bursts). We also care about GPU isolation and predictable tail latency for risk-sensitive features.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with our request patterns and a prod diagram (throughput_requirements.xlsx, finlytics_prod_diagram.png). Would love to get a dedicated demo with someone who can walk us through performance profiles, batching/quantization options, and deployment patterns (VPC/private).

Availability: next week is flexible — mornings PST work best.

Thanks,
Sam Nguyen
Head of Platform
Finlytics
attachments: throughput_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), finlytics_prod_diagram.png (image)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Dedicated for low-latency trading use case

Hi Sam — welcome and thanks for the details, this is exactly the kind of workload Redwood Dedicated is built for.

I looped in Laura (solutions) and Marissa (AE) — Laura can run the throughput/latency deep-dive and show our Dedicated performance profiles, quantization options, and routing/fallback behavior.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue 16 Jun 09:00-09:45
- Tue 16 Jun 11:00-11:45
- Wed 17 Jun 08:30-09:15

If those don't work we can flex — happy to do a 30-45 minute session followed by a technical follow-up. I also added a preliminary HubSpot record here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/finlytics/D-2026-00412

Laura/Marissa — quick ask: can we confirm whether they need GPU-level isolation (single-tenant nodes) vs reserved capacity pooling? Also any red flags from the spreadsheet?

Thanks,
Aditya
SDR, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Dedicated for low-latency trading use case

Thanks for the ping — this looks straightforward but we should prepare a focused demo showing:
- Baseline latency numbers (p50/p95/p99) for 512-token and 128-token payloads on our Dedicated SKU options
- Expected throughput with/without batching and how KV cache/prefix caching affects tail latency
- Quantization trade-offs (8-bit/4-bit) and impact on latency + model quality
- Deployment patterns: reserved single-tenant nodes vs shared reserved pools + routing/fallback

Notes after quick skim of the spreadsheet: their burst profile is spiky (short bursts at 200+ concurrent), sustained lower throughput. We should confirm peak burst duration and whether they can tolerate short throttling or need automatic fallback to a higher-capacity tier.

Marissa — do you want me to prepare the Dedicated-demo deck (dedicated-demo-slides.pdf) and a short perf run with 512-token synthetic traffic? I can run a perf test (30m) and share results prior to the call.

Neha — please sync with infra/solutions to make sure we have a configuration example that meets ~75ms p95 target for 512-token requests if possible. If not, we'll surface expected tail latency and recommended mitigations.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looking forward to the demo — please send a calendar invite.

Best,
